topic: How do distributed satellite constellations impact orbital configuration trade-offs between coverage and inter-satellite interference mitigation?
consensus_response: Distributed satellite constellations significantly impact orbital configuration trade-offs by introducing complex relationships between satellite spacing, orbit altitude, and constellation geometry. As the number of satellites increases, array factor complexity grows, affecting signal quality and interference. Advanced constellation geometries like Walker star or Delta configurations can mitigate inter-satellite interactions while optimizing satellite placement and reducing inter-satellite distances. However, this leads to increased backhaul capacity requirements due to multiple satellites flying over the same area at each time slot, necessitating cooperation between satellite operators and terrestrial networks for centralized interference management.
